archetype.name: Game Manager (spot-duty backup)
archetype.definition: A short-area distributor who wins by completing what the defense gives him underneath and needs a clean, ahead-of-schedule game to produce. He becomes a liability when he has to push the ball into the 10-to-19-yard window.

report.headline: A capable short-game backup whose intermediate throws keep turning into turnovers.
report.take:
Tyson Bagent is Chicago's QB2, and the dossier lists him as the backup as of this week. His 2026 is three cameos stitched together: a relief appearance against Minnesota on 14% of snaps, a full game against the Jets (Case Keenum is credited with that start), and his one start, a 31-7 loss at Green Bay. That is 70 dropbacks. Any read here comes with that caveat, but it lines up closely with his 2023 tape, which makes it more believable than the sample size suggests.

The profile hasn't changed. In 2023 he averaged 6.01 yards an attempt with a 6.2 aDOT and -0.093 EPA a play. This year it's 6.39 YPA, 6.02 intended air yards and -0.069 EPA per dropback. He is accurate and efficient underneath: +0.173 EPA a throw on 0-9 yard passes with a 5.6 CPOE. Rome Odunze has been his best outlet at +0.512 EPA per target. When the game stays short and on schedule, as it did against a Jets defense now ranked 29th (25 of 34, +6.8 EPA), he moves an offense competently.

The damage comes from one band of the field. On 17 intermediate attempts he completed 41.2% with a -13.8 CPOE and threw all three of his interceptions. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, roughly doubled from 2023 (25.45% now against 12.6% then). That reads like a backup forcing it rather than a new skill. The Green Bay start showed the downside: 23.8% bad throws, two picks and -0.361 EPA per dropback. He also has no touchdowns, and the red zone has been empty at -0.296 EPA a play. Part of that is a small-sample drought, and part is a quarterback who doesn't threaten the end zone.

The gap between the jumbled overall line and the two clean games is mostly opponent. He played well against a bad defense and poorly against a good one on the road. That is what a replacement-level backup looks like. Nothing here suggests he would lift the offense if pressed into duty. Nothing suggests a collapse either, as long as the plan keeps him underneath.

strengths.title: Accurate, efficient underneath
strengths.body: His positive value lives on 0-9 yard throws, where he completes passes above expectation and keeps the chains moving. It is the same short-area game he showed as a rookie, so it is a stable trait rather than a hot streak.

strengths.title: Finds Odunze productively
strengths.body: Odunze is the one target he has turned into real value. Most of his passing EPA runs through him, while his other main options sit near zero or below. In any spot start, the plan should lean on that connection.

strengths.title: Low pressure, clean ball security
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 14.7% of dropbacks and hasn't lost a fumble. Some of that is a line that keeps its quarterback upright (the team's offensive hit rate ranks 5th), but it means his issues are decisions, not chaos.

concerns.title: Intermediate window produces turnovers
concerns.body: All three interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, along with a deeply negative CPOE. His tight-window rate has jumped from his 2023 level, which points to forcing throws rather than a reliable skill. This is the real flaw, and it is likely to persist whenever he's asked to push the ball.

concerns.title: No red-zone finishing
concerns.body: He has zero touchdown passes and a -0.296 EPA a play inside the 20. Sixteen plays is too few to call it permanent, but a short-area passer with modest rushing gives defenses little to fear when the field shrinks.

concerns.title: Struggles against real defenses
concerns.body: His one start, at a Green Bay defense now ranked 9th, was a mess, and the Minnesota relief stint against the league's top defense went nowhere. The good numbers came against a bottom-four unit. Expect bad weeks against competent defenses.

trend.note: He went from +6.8 EPA against the Jets to -8.3 at Green Bay a week later, and he hasn't taken a meaningful snap since Caleb Williams returned in Week 6.

nextGame.headline: A soft Lions secondary, but only relevant if he plays
nextGame.body:
Bagent is the backup, and nothing in the dossier says the starter is unavailable. The expectation for Thanksgiving in Detroit is no snaps. If he were pressed into action, though, the matchup suits his game. Detroit ranks 26th against the pass, 27th on short throws, and allows 20.7 PPR points a game to quarterbacks (30th). Tight ends have feasted on them (TE1s run 5.7 points over average, 31st). Detroit also sits 2nd in pass funnel, so offenses throw on them more than usual. The catch is the pass rush: a 4th-ranked sack rate and 5th-ranked hit rate against a quarterback whose pressure-to-sack rate has been poor this year.

On Chicago's side, right tackle-level starter Theo Benedet (75% of snaps) is questionable with a quad injury, and his absence would matter against that rush. Detroit lists safety Chuck Clark (91% snaps) as questionable and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. as out, which further thins a weak coverage group. A four-day turnaround and an indoor game round it out. The 55.5 total says the Book expects points, but that's a Williams-led projection.

keyMatchups.title: His short game vs. Detroit's underneath coverage
keyMatchups.body: Detroit gives up positive EPA on short throws, exactly where Bagent does his best work. If he played, a quick-game plan would play to both sides' tendencies.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit pass rush vs. Benedet's status
keyMatchups.body: The Lions get home often. Bagent has turned 40% of pressures into sacks this season, much worse than his 2023 rate, though on very few plays. A missing tackle would magnify that.

keyMatchups.title: Tight-end funnel, but not with Loveland
keyMatchups.body: Detroit bleeds production to tight ends, yet Bagent's targets to Colston Loveland have been his worst at -0.415 EPA per target. In his hands, that funnel may not cash.

nextGame.watch: Whether the starter's status changes before kickoff; absent that, Bagent is a clipboard holder this week.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is no meaningful stats. He is QB2 behind a healthy starter, and his season line should stay frozen. If he does get starts, expect the same split personality. He'll be efficient underneath with Odunze as the outlet, and he'll give the ball away when he tries to fit throws between 10 and 19 yards. A zero touchdown rate won't last over real volume, but he won't score much either.

In a start, think roughly 150-230 passing yards on 24-34 attempts, with about one interception a game. The range runs higher against soft defenses like the Jets or Detroit and lower against top-10 units. His rushing adds little.
swingFactors: Whether he stays off forced intermediate throws
Opponent quality in any spot starts

confidence.note: 70 dropbacks across three uneven appearances; backup role means future snaps aren't assured.
